stem: When a sample of a radioactive isotope decays by α-particle emission, the α-particles emitted have a single discrete energy. When a sample of a radioactive isotope decays by β⁻ particle emission, the β⁻ particles emitted have a continuous range of energies. What is the explanation for this?

options.A: An antineutrino is emitted with a β⁻ particle but not with an α-particle.
options.B: An antineutrino is emitted with an α-particle but not with a β⁻ particle.
options.C: The α-particles have much more energy than the β⁻ particles.
options.D: The β⁻ particles have much more energy than the α-particles.
